_comment: klt erc supply spec for the digital partition's routed GDS -- the
structural power-delivery read T1 item 11 (klayout-tools#2025, tracked
here as issue #268) grades from. Run it with:
klt erc layout/digital/trng_top.gds layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json \
--top trng_top --format json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` MUST carry `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at Poly2 rather than at Metal1. `active_layer` (Comp) makes
the antenna denominator `poly n diff` instead of raw poly area, which is
what keeps the filltie/endcap/filler cells' gate-less poly bars out of
`gates[]` entirely instead of reporting non-physical antenna ratios for
them (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area').
- Metal1-Metal5 are the conductor order this block's own PDN and routing
use: place-and-route put the followpin straps on Metal1 (0.9 um width,
5.04 um pitch), the row-crossing straps on Metal4 (4.48 um / 44.8 um)
and the top grid on Metal5 (4.48 um / 89.6 um) -- every
`power.straps[].layer` of layout/digital/reports/place_and_route.json is
covered by this stackup, as item 11's digital claim requires. Metal2 and
Metal3 are signal routing; they stay in the stack because the
fabrication order must be contiguous for the via chain to bridge it, but
they carry no supply text of their own.
- `label_layer` only on the two layers this merged GDS actually puts
supply text on -- verified against the stream itself, not assumed:
34/10 carries the gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0 standard cells' own PG pin
text (94 `VDD` + 94 `VSS` labels), 81/10 carries the PDN's top-level
supply pin text (one `vddd` + one `vss`). Metal4's 46/10 text is
signal-pin-only, so declaring it would add nothing.
- GDS layer numbers are gf180mcuD's own drawn-layer numbers (the variant
sim/pdk.json pins), derived from the PDK's own
libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp and cross-checked against
klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck layer table -- both agree on every
entry above.
- `nets[]`: one declared name per physical supply, both `kind: "supply"`,
which is what makes a short between them report as the severe
`erc.supply_short` rather than the general `erc.multiply_driven_net`.
The declared spellings are the 34/10 ones (`VDD`/`VSS`) because those
labels sit on every standard-cell row rail, so a rail-to-grid split
anywhere in the PDN resolves the name to more than one electrical
island and fires `erc.unconnected_net`. The same two islands also
carry the 81/10 spellings `vddd`/`vss` -- this block's authoritative
power_net/ground_net names -- via the top-level PDN pins; declaring
BOTH spellings would report that intentional same-net aliasing as a
false `erc.supply_short`, so the spec declares exactly one name per
supply. Each declared supply resolving to exactly ONE island (zero
`erc.unconnected_net` and zero `erc.supply_short` naming it) is the
pass condition -- a zero count is that verdict, not merely an absence.
- `ties[]` (issue #276): the klayout-tools#2169 false-`erc.supply_short`
collapse that previously forced this spec to omit `ties[]` entirely is
fixed as of klayout-tools#2186 (merged 2026-09-20, shipped in the
0.6.0 release this repo's signoff/check.py pins), which scopes a tie's
well conduction to its own tap sites instead of registering the whole
well region as one blanket conductor. Re-run on that build (verified
live: `klt --version` reports `0.6.0`) declares no false short and no
degenerate tie -- `erc_coverage.skipped` is empty and both entries land
in `erc_coverage.checked` -- so the standing-in netlist-level evidence
this spec used to cite in place of a computed `erc.missing_tie`
(place-and-route's `power.tapcell_master`
gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__filltie plus a matching LVS run) is superseded
by an actual geometric tap check. Two entries, one per physically
distinct well this GDS draws -- both cross-checked against the PDK's
own libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp and klayout-tools' curated
gf180mcu deck layer table, matching the same convention `stackup`
above already follows:
- `nwell_tap` -- gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0's PMOS body: `well_layer`
21/0 (Nwell), `tap_layer` 22/0 (Comp) narrowed by `tap_requires`
32/0 (Nplus) -- `Comp n Nplus` is the real N+ well-strap boolean a
gf180mcu row draws; without the narrowing, bare Comp would also
match every PMOS source/drain diffusion inside the same well (drawn
Comp n Pplus), which is exactly the degenerate declaration
`docs/cli/erc.md`'s 'A degenerate tie is reported as skipped' section
warns against. `connect_to` "Metal1" and `net` "VDD" match this
GDS's own row-rail convention: gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0's cells strap
every N-well tap directly to the Metal1 VDD rail this stackup
already declares.
- `pwell_tap` -- the same row's NMOS body. This library draws its
P-type body region as its own marker layer rather than leaving it a
bare, undrawn substrate: `well_layer` 204/0 (LVPWELL -- the PDK's
own name for this marker; verified present in the merged GDS, 94
shapes, one per Nwell-adjacent row), `tap_layer` 22/0 (Comp)
narrowed by `tap_requires` 31/0 (Pplus) -- `Comp n Pplus` is the P+
substrate/well-strap boolean, the same reasoning as `nwell_tap`
mirrored to the other doping. `connect_to` "Metal1" and `net`
"VSS", matching the VSS rail the same way.
Both resolve to `erc.missing_tie` computed and zero -- see
layout/digital/reports/erc-supply.json's own `erc_coverage.checked`
and `provenance.klt_version` for the run this claim rests on.
`net: "VDD"`/`"VSS"` (not `"vddd"`/`"vss"`) matches this spec's own
`nets[]` choice above and the same reasoning: the 34/10 rail-label
spelling is what every standard-cell row -- and therefore every tap
site -- actually sits on, and it resolves to the same electrical
island as `vddd`/`vss` per the `nets[]` note above, so declaring the
tie against `VDD`/`VSS` checks the identical net a `vddd`/`vss`
declaration would, without re-raising the dual-spelling aliasing
`nets[]` above already explains avoiding.
